meta.title: Speech, Voice & Realtime Model Field Guide
meta.subtitle: GPT speech/voice/realtime catalog + a grounded six-model realtime transcription pilot
meta.disclaimer: Private/internal artifact. Costs are OpenAI public list rates (2026-10-14), NOT a verified Azure bill. Measured facts come from this pilot's saved evidence; documented facts come from vendor docs; not_tested / unknown are shown as such.

cards.name: gpt-live-1
cards.headline: Full-duplex voice agent frontend — listens while it speaks.
cards.what: A speech-to-speech voice agent that can listen while speaking (full duplex). It delegates reasoning and tool calls to a separate backend model, which is billed separately.
cards.tested_detail: Caldova's voice path explicitly uses gpt-live-1. That functional voice test is SEPARATE from the six-model transcription benchmark; gpt-live-1 was not one of the six transcription models.
cards.diarization: not a transcription model; no meeting-diarization claim

cost.note: Plus separate backend reasoning + tool charges — not included.

cards.name: gpt-realtime
cards.headline: Conversational realtime model (base), prompted to transcribe.
cards.what: A streaming conversational voice model (voice / input-text / image). In this pilot it was PROMPTED to emit a transcript with textual Speaker A/B labels — it is NOT a dedicated transcription model and has NO native meeting diarization.
cards.diarization: none native; speaker labels are prompted generation

cards.name: MAI-Transcribe-2
cards.headline: Microsoft batch transcription — full-file speaker IDs, per-request only.
cards.what: Azure MAI batch transcription. Full 28-min file returned HTTP 200 in 20.6s with 92 phrases / 4486 words and 8 unique speaker IDs (0–7) — NOT verified against 8 real people. Rich config (word timestamps + clean style + phrase-list hints + en-US) returned HTTP 200; default is verbatim. maxSpeakers was rejected (400); confidence 0 returned, not usable. No documented cross-request session ID / references / reusable embeddings.
cards.diarization: per-file speaker IDs; IDs restart every request (no cross-request matching)

cost.note: Advertised introductory rate on the Microsoft model page — NOT an Azure bill.

cards.name: MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming
cards.headline: MAI streaming — works, but no diarization.
cards.what: MAI streaming via Sweden SDK 1.52. Works, but NO diarization. An earlier 15s audio took 34.6s to finalize — the advertised ~120ms was not verified.

cost.note: Advertised introductory stream rate (Microsoft model page) — NOT an Azure bill.

cards.name: Azure ConversationTranscriber (rttold)
cards.headline: Classic continuous diarization — best observed continuity.
cards.what: Azure classic continuous ConversationTranscriber, the `rttold` default. Produced the best observed speaker continuity in this pilot, with brief turn mistakes, and its own wording quirks (e.g. 'chatbot Brad' where MAI said 'RAG'). Like the 30s MAI request, it placed the introduction under one speaker. Default `rttold` = classic continuous, left UNCHANGED.
cards.diarization: continuous speaker labels (best continuity observed here)

cost.note: Azure rate NOT reverified — verify Azure quote; not $0/free.

methodology.fixture: Same source test.mp3 seconds 300–330 (30s), decoded once to mono PCM16 24kHz.
methodology.commits: Two 15-second commits in ONE retained conversational session.
methodology.pacing: Audio paced at source speed (100ms frames); English; text output.
methodology.settings: Same transcription-only instructions, VAD disabled, provider-default reasoning, no vocabulary hints / corrections / references.
methodology.reps: Three repetitions per model; six models × 6 attempts (two auth routes × 3).
methodology.auth: Both auth routes attempted SEPARATELY: ephemeral minted key vs direct AAD. 26 of 36 attempts were setup failures (timeouts / HTTP 408, including mint + WS).
methodology.scoring: Targeted diagnostics (Frank continuity, three-voices-distinct, latency), NOT WER/DER. No whole-meeting winner.
methodology.latency_caveat: 'First text after commit' includes deliberate 15s accumulation; it is NOT minimum model latency.
methodology.base_outlier: gpt-realtime median 0.597s but range reaches 18.597s — the outlier MUST stay visible; do not rank on median alone.
methodology.confound: Earlier 2.1 runs were on Caldova; others on temporary PAYG deployments. Both East US 2, but the account difference is a timing confound.
methodology.earlier_pilot: An earlier 2.1 initial-pilot success is NOT included in this 36-attempt aggregate.
methodology.shortlist: 1.5 and 2.1 are TENTATIVE shortlist candidates only — full-meeting validation pending.

benchmark.denominator_rule: Passes are over COMPLETED runs, not attempts. No quality scores exist for setup-failed runs.

full_file.caveat: 8 unique IDs — NOT verified as 8 distinct people.

chunked_excerpt.issue: Speaker IDs restart per request. Speaker 0 assigned to multiple distinct self-introductions and both sides of dialogue. No cross-chunk matching.

chunk_15_vs_10.note: 15s chunks do NOT solve cross-request label reset.

concepts.voice_agent: A voice agent (gpt-live-1) holds a spoken conversation — it listens while it speaks (full duplex) and delegates reasoning/tools to a backend. It is not a transcriber.
concepts.asr: ASR / transcription turns speech into text. Diarization additionally labels WHO spoke. Some endpoints do neither speaker labeling (e.g. gpt-live-transcribe).
concepts.tts: TTS turns text into spoken audio (e.g. gpt-4o-mini-tts). The reverse direction of ASR.
concepts.streamed_vs_continuous: Streamed file / committed-turn output processes a bounded chunk and RESETS speaker labels each request. Continuous audio (classic ConversationTranscriber) keeps one session and carries speaker identity across the stream — which is why it showed the best continuity here.
concepts.realtime_prompted: The six GPT-Realtime models are conversational models PROMPTED to emit Speaker A/B text. That is generated labeling, not native diarization.
concepts.aliases: rtt (openai 10s chunks), rttold (classic continuous), rttheb (Azure LLM Speech). Tested paths vs unverified paths are marked per card.
